_method_note: Machine-readable source of truth for what exists in the world. Fed by three sources: material (excavated evidence via /integrate), tale (knowledge authored directly by the user), and hearsay (claims made by characters in scenes). Characters sample their knowledge from these categories. Each entry carries sources documenting where it came from.

location.description: Places: cities, regions, landmarks, anything with geographic or cultural significance.

character.description: Named people: in-world inhabitants, legendary or historical figures, real-world authors and players.

concept.description: Ideas and abstract things: philosophies, beliefs, systems, immaterial constructs.

conflict.description: Unresolved disagreements: contradictions between sources, open questions about the record.

route.description: Ways between places: roads, highways, train lines, air routes, established paths.

time_systems.description: Time references: units of time, named periods, timelines, eras.

hearsay.description: Claims made by characters in scenes: what people have said. Each claim may reference other entries in encodings.

tale.description: Oral tradition: knowledge authored directly by the user, stated as fact or narrated as story.
